# Setting Up
```{r}
#| label: Set-Up
#| warning: false
#| echo: true

## Load in dataset

library("here")
library("tidyverse")
library("tidytuesdayR")

if (!dir.exists(here("data"))) {
    dir.create(here("data"))
}

b_lyrics <- readRDS(here("data", "b_lyrics.RDS"))
ts_lyrics <- readRDS(here("data", "ts_lyrics.RDS"))
sales <- readRDS(here("data", "sales.RDS"))

rds_files <- c("b_lyrics.RDS", "ts_lyrics.RDS", "sales.RDS")
## Check whether we have all 3 files
if (any(!file.exists(here("data", rds_files)))) {
    ## If we don't, then download the data
    b_lyrics <- readr::read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/master/data/2020/2020-09-29/beyonce_lyrics.csv")
    ts_lyrics <- readr::read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/master/data/2020/2020-09-29/taylor_swift_lyrics.csv")
    sales <- readr::read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/master/data/2020/2020-09-29/sales.csv")

    ## Then save the data objects to RDS files
    saveRDS(b_lyrics, file = here("data", "b_lyrics.RDS"))
    saveRDS(ts_lyrics, file = here("data", "ts_lyrics.RDS"))
    saveRDS(sales, file = here("data", "sales.RDS"))
}
```

# Part 1: Explore Album Sales 
## Part 1A: 
```{r}
#| label: Part 1A
#| warning: false
#| echo: true

glimpse(sales)

sales_tidy <- sales |>
    ## Removes "extra stuff" from datesm then convert use stringr to get date (includes regular expression)
    mutate(
        released = str_remove(released, " \\([A-Z]+\\)\\[[0-9]+\\]"),
        released = mdy(released)
    ) |>
    ## Use forcats to create a factor called country 
    mutate(country = fct_collapse(country,
        "World" = c("World", "WW"),
        "FRA"   = c("FRA", "FR")
    )) |>
    ## Convert sales to album sales in millions of dollars.
    mutate(sales = sales / 1000000) |>
    ## Keep only album sales from the UK, the US or the World
    filter(country %in% c("UK", "US", "World"))

## Auto print your final wrangled tibble data frame.
sales_tidy



```

## Part 1B: 
```{r}
#| label: Part 1B
#| warning: false
#| echo: true

sales_us <- sales_tidy |>
    ## Keep only US states
    filter(country == "US") |>
    ## Get release years and go to whole number (source below)
    mutate(
        years_since_release = floor(interval(released, today()) / years(1))
    )

sales_us

## Group by Artist, summarizing by most recent, oldest, and median years since release by artist
sales_us |>
    group_by(artist) |>
    summarize(
        most_recent = min(years_since_release),
        oldest      = max(years_since_release),
        median      = median(years_since_release)
    )
```

Sources I used to help me complete this: 

https://lubridate.tidyverse.org/reference/interval.html

https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/base/versions/3.6.2/topics/Round

## Part 1C 
```{r}
#| label: Part 1C
#| warning: false
#| echo: true

## Get total album sales in millions by artist and country using Part 1A data
total_sales <- sales_tidy |>
    group_by(artist, country) |>
    ## Added .groups = drops from error in console 
    summarize(total_sales = sum(sales), .groups = "drop")
total_sales

##  Creating a percent stacked bar chart
total_sales |>
    ## Setting aes with x and y respectively, incorporating info for stacked bar chart 
    ggplot(aes(x = artist, y = total_sales, fill = country)) +
    geom_bar(position = "fill", stat = "identity") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    ## Settinf labels 
    labs(
        title = "Studio album sales by country",
        subtitle = "Beyoncé vs. Taylor Swift (UK, US, and World)",
        x = "Artist",
        y = "Percentage of total album sales (millions)",
        fill = "Country"
    )
```

Sources I used to help me complete this: 

https://r-graph-gallery.com/48-grouped-barplot-with-ggplot2

https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/scale_continuous.html

## Part 1D
```{r}
#| label: Part 1D
#| warning: false
#| echo: true

## Data from 1A
sales_tidy |>
    ## Filtering for Wold 
    filter(country == "World") |>
    ## including forcats functions 
    mutate(title = fct_reorder(title, sales)) |>
    ## Creating chart 
    ggplot(aes(x = sales, y = title, fill = artist)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
    ## Creating labels 
    labs(
        title = "Worldwide sales of studio albums",
        subtitle = "Albums organized by worldwide sales (in millions)\nfor Beyoncé and Taylor Swift",
        x = "Album sales (millions)",
        y = "Album title",
        fill = "Artist"
    ) + 
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) + 
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

```

## Part 1E
```{r}
#| label: Part 1E
#| warning: false
#| echo: true

## Data from Part 1A
sales_tidy |>
    ## Setting x, y, and color
    ggplot(aes(x = released, y = sales, color = artist)) +
    ## Setting point size
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    ## Using facet by rows (stacked)
    facet_grid(country ~ .) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y")+ 
    ## Setting labels 
    labs(
        title = "Studio album sales by release date",
        x = "Release date",
        y = "Album sales (millions)",
        color = "Artist"
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
        )
```

Sources I used to help me complete this: 

https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/scale_date.html
